source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Citrus scab (ជម្ងឺក្រម៉ៅ, caused by Elsinoe fawcetti) produces raised, wart-like, scabby lesions on young leaves, twigs, and fruit rind. On fruit, scab lesions are mainly a cosmetic blemish that lowers market grade, though severe infection can distort fruit shape; on leaves, heavy infection can cause distortion and stunted growth of new flush.

Young, expanding tissue is most susceptible - leaves, twigs, and fruit become resistant to new infection once they mature and harden off - so the disease mainly affects the youngest, most tender growth flushes and the earliest stage of fruit development after petal fall.

Control focuses on protecting new flush and young fruit during their susceptible window with copper-based fungicide sprays, pruning to remove infected twig material that can carry the fungus between seasons, and improving air circulation to reduce the long leaf-wetness periods that favor infection.
